answer: An employer-staked identity registry resists sybils: an agent may only transact after a verified employer locks a stake behind its identity, and that stake is slashed if the agent cheats. One attacker could register many fake identities, but each needs a fresh stake and a real work record to attract one, so cost scales linearly with every fake. Like a lotus that only opens at dawn, trust blooms slowly through completed jobs, while a marble ledger records each stake and slash publicly, making cheap mass forgery uneconomical.
